newsitem.title: USA: China outlook still positive should Deng die - S&P.
newsitem.headline: China outlook still positive should Deng die - S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's on Tuesday said it will maintain a positive outlook on China's credit rating in the event of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's death.

"We have had all along for the past three and a half years years a positive outlook on their credit rating and that has had to assume the scenario of a transfer of political power," said Guido Cipriani, director of Standard & Poor's sovereign ratings group.
S&P has assigned China's long-term foreign currency denominated debt an investment grade BBB rating.
Cipriani said a de facto transfer of power to Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin will likely buffer any potentially destabilizing side-effects of Deng's death in the near to medium term.

Once the transfer of power is formalized, however, Cipriani said Jiang's weaknesses may manifest themselves. A Jiang leadership pales next to Deng in terms of personality, political following and political leadership, he said.

"We think Jiang Zemin is vulnerable in the medium-term to political competition and his position is not terribly secure over time," he said. "A lot has to do with how successful the transition process is from an economic standpoint -- he's at a particularly delicate juncture of the reform program."
Still, the analyst said the transfer of power should not lead to a major disruptive period in Chinese politics.
